issues.description: The problem statement (UML and textual description) declares messageOnMilk() as returning a boolean (and describes returning true/false), but the provided solution and the template's example usage treat messageOnMilk() as returning a String (the solution's Milkable interface and Goat/Seal implementations return descriptive strings). This mismatch between the specification and the reference implementation will confuse students about the correct return type and what to implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Resolve the mismatch by choosing one return type and aligning all artifacts. Recommended: update the problem statement (UML and textual description) to specify that messageOnMilk() returns String (and provide an example string), since the solution and the example usage in Main expect and print a textual message. Alternatively, change the solution and template example to use boolean-returning messageOnMilk() and adjust tests/instructions to describe the boolean semantics.

issues.description: The problem statement/UML specifies that Milkable.messageOnMilk() returns a boolean (milking success), but the reference implementation defines Milkable.messageOnMilk() returning a String and Goat/Seal implementations return textual messages. This mismatch of the same method's contract across artifacts creates confusion about the expected API and return semantics.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the contract for messageOnMilk() across problem statement, template, and solution. Either: (A) change the problem statement/UML text to specify messageOnMilk(): String and describe it as returning a milking message (and update any textual description accordingly), or (B) change the solution (Milkable interface and Goat/Seal implementations) to return boolean and adjust usages (e.g., Main and tests) to handle booleans. Prefer aligning to one return type and updating all artifacts so students have a single, consistent API to implement.
